data.long_meaning: Derived from the Slavic words 'zlat' (gold) and 'mira' (peace). Refers to the peaceful and golden nature of the name. in_greek.name: Ζλατομίρα
in_greek.long_meaning: Η Ζλατομίρα είναι όνομα που προέρχεται από τη σύνθεση δύο λέξεων: 'ζλατός' που σημαίνει χρυσός και 'μίρα' που σημαίνει πολύτιμος. Το όνομα αυτό έχει τις ρίζες του στα ελληνικά και εβραϊκά και συμβολίζει την πολύτιμη και λαμπερή αξία.

in_latin.name: Zlatomira
in_latin.long_meaning: Nomen Zlatomira derivatur ex duabus vocibus: 'zlatos' quod significat aurum et 'mira' quod significat pretiosus. Hoc nomen oritur ex radicibus hebraicis et graecis et significat valorem pretiosum et splendidum.

in_english.name: Zlatomira
in_english.meaning: Zlatomira - a precious and golden treasure
in_english.long_meaning: The name Zlatomira is derived from the combination of two words: 'zlatos' meaning gold and 'mira' meaning precious. With roots in Hebrew and Greek, the name symbolizes a valuable and shining treasure. Although not directly mentioned in the Bible, the components of the name reflect biblical themes of preciousness and divine value. Historically, the name has been used in Christian traditions to signify a cherished and luminous heritage. The personality traits associated with Zlatomira include being radiant, valuable, and spiritually significant.

data.cultural_impact: The name Zlatomira has cultural significance in various Slavic countries, especially in Eastern Europe, where it is a rare yet beautiful name. This name embodies the idea of appreciating the beauty of life with peace, tranquility, and a golden disposition. In some regions, it is also associated with ancient Slavic gods, particularly Perun, the god of thunder, lightning, and the heavens, and Peruna, the goddess of the forest, water, and fertility, who were revered for their golden aura and supreme power.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Zlatomira implies the pursuit of inner peace, serenity, and the blessings of divine providence. It may also symbolize the attainment of the golden mean in life, striking a balance between various aspects of existence, and recognizing the value of every moment. Ultimately, this name may serve as a reminder to cherish the beauty of life while striving for spiritual emanations of peace and tranquility, transcending earthly material and transient aspects.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Zlatomira, meaning "Golden Peace," embodies the inner tranquility and radiance of the soul. It is a reminder of the precious gift of peace that can be found in the midst of life's challenges, illuminating the journey towards spiritual growth.

historical_references.reference: According to Slavic mythology, Zlatomira was the goddess of wealth and gold. She was also believed to protect crops and fields from harm. Her name translates to 'Golden-mermaid'. This goddess was revered in the regions of present-day Slovakia, Hungary, and Romania during the early Slavic period (5th-7th centuries AD).

During the Middle Ages in Bulgaria, there was a female saint named Saint Zlatomira. She was believed to have been martyred during the Roman persecutions of Christians in the 3rd or 4th century AD. Her relics were later discovered in the 13th century and were enshrined in the Church of Saint Demetrius in the city of Devina. She is still revered as a patron saint of wealth and gold in Bulgarian Orthodox Christianity.
